title: The twelve sent out (Luke 9:1–17)
hook: sent with nothing, then the five thousand fed
carry: you give them something to eat

segments.voice: Yesterday, a woman in the crowd and a girl who got up and ate. Your line was only believe. Did you do one small thing for the quiet one of your two? Day five hundred thirty-four.

No walking stick, no bag, no bread, no money, no spare clothes. That's the packing list Jesus gives the twelve. In the King James words: "Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece." A scrip is a traveler's bag. So they go out empty-handed, village by village, to preach and to heal, depending on whoever opens a door. Until now they've watched. Now they're sent. And it works. Word spreads so far that Herod himself, who had John beheaded, hears about it and is perplexed. Who is this? He wants to see him.
screen: `NO STAFF, NO BAG, NO BREAD, NO MONEY.`

segments.voice: The twelve come back full of stories, and Jesus takes them aside privately, to a deserted place near a town called Bethsaida. But the crowds follow. Luke says Jesus "received them," welcomed them, spoke about the kingdom, healed those who needed it. Hours pass. The sun gets low. And the twelve, sensibly, come to him: "Send the multitude away, that they may go into the towns and country round about, and lodge, and get victuals: for we are here in a desert place." It's a reasonable plan. It's what any good organizer would say. And Jesus answers, short and plain: "Give ye them to eat." You. You feed them. They've just come back from a journey where they carried nothing. Now he hands the problem back to them. They count what they have: "We have no more but five loaves and two fishes." About five thousand men, Luke says. Jesus has them sit down in groups of about fifty, like guests at a meal. Then he takes the five loaves and two fish, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and gives to the disciples to set before the crowd. Later in Luke, at the Last Supper, nearly the same movements return: took, gave thanks, broke, gave. Everyone eats. Everyone is filled. And they pick up the leftovers: twelve baskets. Some readers notice: one for each of the twelve who said send them away. Jesus didn't do it without them. He did it through their hands, with what they already had, which was almost nothing.
screen: then, large: `GIVE YE THEM TO EAT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: go without one comfort today. Settle, and breathe. The twelve went out with nothing extra and found they had enough. Think of one small comfort you could set aside for a day: the second coffee, the snack, the streaming show, the online shopping, the extra blanket of scrolling before sleep. Not as punishment. As a way of noticing how much you usually carry. Picture the day without it. Then think: what could that small saving, of money or time, become in someone else's hands? A meal, a gift, an hour for someone. Five loaves and two fish. If you pray, you can offer that small thing to God. If you don't, simply decide where it goes. The bell holds the time.
Scrip, an old word for a traveler's bag: Jesus sends the twelve out with nothing, then hands them a hungry crowd and five loaves, and through their hands five thousand are fed.
Your line: you give them something to eat. Skip your one comfort today, and let what it saves feed someone. Day five hundred thirty-four.

howItsDone: Some Christian food pantries and church meal programs take "give ye them to eat" as a motto, and Christians often notice in this meal the actions of the Last Supper and communion: taking, blessing, breaking and giving bread.

fork.setup: you're one of the twelve. it's late, you're in a deserted place, and there are thousands of hungry people. what do you suggest?
options: send them away to find food and lodging.
ask what we have and bring it to Jesus.
fork.reveal: the disciples said send them away. Jesus answered: give ye them to eat. and their five loaves and two fish fed everyone.

original.note: Greek: you give them to eat. the "you" is emphatic.

trapdoor: what you thought: Jesus fed five thousand people by himself.
what it means: he hands the problem to the disciples, takes their almost-nothing, and feeds everyone through their hands.
what a scholar hears: took, blessed, broke and gave are nearly the actions Luke repeats at the Last Supper, where Jesus gives thanks, so readers hear that meal ahead in this one.

notes: Greek of 9:13 (dote autois humeis phagein) and the emphatic humeis. Confirm.
'That's not counting everyone': Luke says about five thousand men (andres); Matthew 14:21 adds 'beside women and children'. Confirm framing.
Fork answer is the disciples' actual suggestion (send them away), as the guide asks for the text's real answer.
Twelve baskets matching the twelve disciples is an observation, not something Luke states.
